tldr: Headlines across 12 outlet clusters uniformly report the Kolkata hotel fire as a death-toll event — nine dead, six injured — but diverge sharply on victim identity: Indian outlets lead with 'Bangladeshi nationals killed' while international wire services and European titles stay nationality-neutral; two English-language Asian outlets (Malay Mail, SCMP) are the only headlines to name a suspected cause (AC explosion), surfacing an infrastructure angle visible nowhere else above the fold.

single_outlet_findings.finding: Only headline to name a suspected physical cause ('AC explosion') and label the event 'latest India hotel fire disaster' — framing it as a recurring pattern rather than an isolated incident, a systemic signal absent from all other titles above the fold.

Leads headline with 'budget hotel' and 'air-con explosion' — foregrounding the venue's socioeconomic class and infrastructure failure, while Indian domestic headlines foreground victim nationality instead.

Only non-Indian outlet to flag victim identity in the headline, but uses the generic 'nine foreigners' (иностранцев) rather than 'Bangladeshi nationals' — preserving the outsider angle while erasing national specificity.

One of two ARY News headlines in this cluster is entirely off-topic (a Karachi police encounter with alleged dacoits at index 2), confirming cluster noise from a broad domestic Pakistan feed pull alongside the on-topic hotel-fire item.

bottom_line: The headline layer reduces this tragedy almost universally to a death count, but the sharpest editorial choice — whether to name the victims as Bangladeshis or leave them nationality-neutral — divides Indian domestic outlets from the international press at the very first line of coverage.
